content.title: Team USA runs out of steam in falling to Venezuela in 2026 WBC final
content.text: Updated March 17, 2026, 11:42 p.m. ETIt was Venezuela that proved it was built for the grand stage of the World Baseball Classic championship game.Up against the star-studded United States lineup, Venezuela’s pitching staff did not back down. They rose up, limiting the U.S. hitters to two runs on three hits.When Bryce Harper delivered an electric, game-tying two-run home run in the eighth inning, the Venezuelans manufactured an immediate answer.Eugenio Suarez banged a ninth-inning RBI double to lift Venezuela to the World Baseball Classic title with a 3-2 victory over the United States on Tuesday night at loanDepot Park in Miami.In the end, Venezuela's fire, passion and pride were on full display as they took down defending champion Japan, up-starts Italy, and the United States powerhouse en route to their first WBC title.For the majority of the game, the potent United States offense looked feeble. Through seven innings, it had only mustered a pair of singles and two walks, highlighted by Eduardo Rodriguez’s sterling 4⅓ innings out of the gate.That allowed Venezuela to jump out to a 2-0 lead through five innings behind a Maikel Garcia sacrifice fly and Wilyer Abreu solo home run off the Mets' Nolan McLean. That squeezed the United States' comeback attempt to two final innings, but it turned out that Venezuela would not be denied on this night.Here was our analysis from throughout the game:Eugenio Suarez lifts Venezuela to brink of title in ninthAfter the United States tied the game, Venezuela mounted an immediate response.With Garrett Whitlock on for the ninth inning, Luis Arraez drew a walk and Venezuela manager Omar Lopez made a heads-up substitution to bring on Javier Sanoja.Sanoja stole second base on a bang-bang play that was upheld upon review, and Eugenio Suarez put Venezuela ahead 3-2 with an RBI double into the left-center field gap.Bryce Harper's big swing, tying HR shocks USA to lifeIn a flash, Bryce Harper jolted the Team USA offense to life with the nation staring down an epic let down.After the United States could only muster two hits and two walks through seven scoreless innings against Venezuela, it only took one swing from the Phillies superstar to flip the championship on its head.Staring down a runner-up finish with five outs remaining, Bobby Witt drew a walk against Andres Machado and Harper tattooed a game-tying two-run home run to center field on a hanging changeup.In an instant, the United States' offense's futility is erased. We're tied 2-2 heading to the ninth.Team USA bullpen holding up its endThe one major element lacking from the U.S. in the WBC championship game is its offense, because it's pitching staff has certainly held up its end of the bargain.Behind Nolan McLean, the USA bullpen has delivered to keep their team within striking distance at 2-0 after the top of the eighth inning.The trio of Brad Keller, Will Vest and Griffin Jax have held Venezuela at bay between the fifth and eighth innings. They have combined to toss 3⅓ scoreless innings with three strikeouts. Ezequiel Tovar delivered Venezuela's lone hit against the U.S. bullpen — a seventh inning single against Vest.Team USA lineup going quietlyThe United States is nine outs away from being shut out in the championship game of the World Baseball Classic.Through six innings, the U.S. has only two hits and one walk against the Venezuela trio of Eduardo Rodriguez, Eduard Bazardo and Jose Butto.The USA had a major opportunity in the top of the sixth after Bryce Harper singled through the right side of the infield. Aaron Judge worked the count full against Butto but bounced out to third base on a slider over the heart of the plate.Venezuela leads 2-0 heading to the seventh inning.Eduardo Rodriguez shoves for Venezuela in WBC championship gameVenezuela could not have asked for more from their left-hander, Eduardo Rodriguez, in the championship game.The Diamondbacks starting pitcher only allowed two USA baserunners in 4⅓ innings to help his team build a 2-0 lead in the bottom of the fifth.The only U.S. traffic against the Venezuela starter was a one-out single to Brice Turang in the bottom of the third inning and a two-out walk to Kyle Schwarber in the bottom of the fourth. Rodriguez struck out four.Wilyer Abreu keeps dream WBC run going, adds to Venezuela leadRed Sox outfielder Wilyer Abreu has delivered some of the biggest offensive fireworks for Venezuela throughout the WBC.In the quarterfinals against Japan, Abreu launched a go-ahead three-run home run to punctuate their 8-5 win. In the championship game on Tuesday night, Abreu added another memory, tagging a 414-foot solo home run to straightaway center field off Nolan McLean in the top of the fifth inning.The long ball moved Venezuela ahead 2-0 after the top of the fourth inning.After the home run, McLean picked up back-to-back outs against Salvador Perez and Jackson Chourio. With the top of the Venezuela lineup looming, McLean exited with two earned runs allowed on four hits and one walk in 4⅔ innings. The Mets starter threw 63 pitches.U.S. gets first hit off Eduardo Rodriguez, nothing moreThe United States has been aggressive against Eduardo Rodriguez but does not have much to show for it through three innings.Brice Turang tagged the first hit with one out in the third inning but that is the only offensive production for the USA. Rodriguez has struck out three, picked up two ground balls and three fly outs in three frames. He's thrown 35 pitches.Venezuela strikes first on sacrifice flyVenezuela put the pressure on against Nolan McLean in the third inning, with Salvador Perez shooting an opposite-field single and Ronald Acuña Jr. drawing a one-out walk.A wild pitch from McLean moved both runners into scoring position and Maikel Garcia moved Venezuela ahead 1-0 on a sacrifice fly to center field.McLean, who said he expected to throw around 65-70 pitches, has thrown 37 pitches through three innings.Nolan McLean looking dialed in through twoI think it's safe to say that the adrenaline is pumping for McLean, who is regularly touching 99 mph with his fastball in the first two innings. (He averaged 95.8 mph in eight starts with the Mets last season).McLean seems to have a feel for his tight spin, as well, striking out Eugenio Suarez chasing a sweeper and Gleyber Torres looking on a curveball.The two strikeouts are worth another look:The Mets starter worked around a bloop single by popping up Wilyer Abreu to keep things scoreless through the top of the second.Eduardo Rodriguez answers with his own 1-2-3 inningWhere's the ABS? Even U.S. manager Mark DeRosa said he expects the automated ball-strike system to be deployed at the next World Baseball Classic after a controversial final strikeout call ended the Dominican Republic's run in the semifinals.Aaron Judge might have liked it to be there in the opening inning as he was froze on a called strike three on a cutter that may or may not have caught the corner.The strikeout capped a 1-2-3 inning for Venezuela's Eduardo Rodriguez, who picked up fly balls from Bobby Witt Jr. and Bryce Harper to begin his outing.A quick shutout inning for Nolan McLeanThe pressure could have mounted right away for Nolan McLean, who was tagged for a leadoff single by Ronald Acuña Jr. on the first pitch of the game.McLean answered with the best possible result, getting Maikel Garcia to bounce into a double play to Alex Bregman at third base. Then, the USA starter got Luis Arraez to pop-up on a high 99 mph fastball.The opening frame took McLean all of five pitches.USA lineup vs Venezuela in World Baseball Classic finalEmbedded content: https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/mlb/2026/03/17/usa-lineup-venezuela-world-baseball-classic-2026-today-final/89194697007/U.S. manager Mark DeRosa had some decisions to make with the left-handed Eduardo Rodriguez on the mound.Despite Gunnar Henderson providing an offensive spark in the infield, with six hits so far, DeRosa decided to go with the right-handed hitting Alex Bregman at third base. Bregman has a history against Rodriguez tagging nine hits in 27 at-bats in his career against the southpaw.The U.S. manager went with the same line of thinking in center field, electing to go with the right-handed hitting Byron Buxton instead of the hot-hitting, albeit from the left side, Pete Crow-Armstrong.With Cal Raleigh struggling to an 0-for-9 clip thus far in the tournament, the U.S. skipper elected to go with Will Smith behind the plate.Venezuela lineup vs USA in World Baseball Classic finalTeam USA players arrive wearing USA Olympic hockey jerseysThe U.S. players arrived at the stadium for tonight's World Baseball Classic championship game wearing a United States Olympic men’s hockey jerseys. Here's a look at Team USA captain Aaron Judge:And here's Nolan McLean of the Mets, tonight's starting pitcher for Team USA:Nolan McLean hungry for big opportunityWhen Mark DeRosa was filling out the USA roster, Nolan McLean's competitive fire drew an endorsement from Matt Holliday, an assistant coach with Oklahoma State and the U.S.Now, the 24-year-old right-hander will have an opportunity to showcase what the former major leaguer boasted about in the championship game, despite only pitching in eight major league games in his career."I think as a competitor and as someone if you work your whole life at something, you want to be put in these spots," McLean said. "It's just kind of a dream come true to be able to get the ball in such a big moment and something I want to do."McLean, who's primed to step into a bigger role for the Mets this season, will be looking to shake off a uneven start against Italy when he allowed three earned runs on a pair of home runs and struck out four across three innings.What time is USA vs Venezuela today in World Baseball Classic?Date: Tuesday, March 17Time: 8 p.m.What channel is USA vs Venezuela today in World Baseball Classic?TV: FOXWatch USA vs Venezuela live on Fubo
